after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,0),(1,5),(2,3).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{\pi /2}$ by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians about the origin?

- $(-5,1)$
- $(0,-2)$
- $(2,-3)$
after.worked_solution:
The counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{\pi /2}$ by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians is given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{\pi /2},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{\pi /2}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(0,0),(-5,1),(-3,2).$

So, the correct answer is "I only."

Consider the vector $v$ shown above. Find the vector $Av$ given that 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors. Computing the images of ${i,j}$ under $A$, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =Ai=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j \\ {j}^{′} & =Aj=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068585/assets/f154267ed0a528b1e9fbec40064b090560410fe76dab00070e13fb3d1978b59c.png)

So, the matrix represents a rotation of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin.

Therefore, in order to find $Av$, we need to rotate $v$ counterclockwise by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068585/assets/dd0496914b35f969896c6a54907fbfa5ea6c139c878d8682b933a8757bde7524.png)

after.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${270}^{∘}$ is the same as counterclockwise rotation by an angle of ${90}^{∘}.$ It's given by the matrix

$$
R[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(1,1),(-3,-2),(0,-1).$

So, the correct answer is "I and II only."
